author: Alex Prieto-Rivero
title: First Reformed Church awarded FEMA grant for June 2024 flood recovery - NewsBreak
text:
By Alex Prieto-Rivero ,
2 hours ago
ROCK VALLEY , Iowa ( KCAU ) — The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) has awarded grants to several community organizations, including the First Reformed Church in Rock Valley, Iowa.
“We flooded like everybody else did,” said Public Works Director and church member Myron Van Ginkel. “We had about a foot and a half in the main part, in the lower part of the church, and the full basement.”
Van Ginkel submitted the application for assistance to FEMA.
Story continues below
“It’s a huge process of paperwork to do and to complete before you’re obligated and get money,” said Van Ginkel.
The church was awarded $370,157 to help repair damage to the church building.
“Our fellowship hall is about three feet lower than our actual sanctuary. Most of the damage was done into the fellowship hall. In the basement, we had all the Sunday school rooms and the youth room. All of that was destroyed,” said Van Ginkel.
Van Ginkel said that he is happy he applied for the funds to help with recovery efforts.
“Every little bit helps. It’s a lot of paperwork, but if you don’t do it, you get nothing. So, it’s definitely worth the time and effort,” Van Ginkel said.
